measuredBy: hoofdbureau rework lane, 2026-10-13: read off the rectified panorama crops of `landmark-brief.ts` (artifacts/landmark-briefs/hoofdbureau-elandsgracht/, Gemeente Amsterdam panoramas CC BY 4.0) with the metre grid of `elevation-grid.ts`; not counted blind, not guessed. Values marked in `inferred` lists are not visible in any crop.
frame: s = metres along the photographed wall from its viewer-left corner (the crop's left edge, `Wall.a` of pand-reference); y = metres above the 3DBAG ground (crop bottom row) after the crop's `yShift`. On the builder's panel: u = s + sToU (hoofdbureau-elandsgracht-walls.ts prints the panels and offsets).

w16-337.what: north end wall of the Marnixstraat wing on the Elandsgracht: the Amsterdam arms relief, banner, three Krop figures, six round windows, open ground storey on four columns
w16-337.registration: parapet top 16.72 m in the crop vs 3DBAG 16.96 m: crop heights kept as read (0.24 m inside the tolerance of a 24 m camera)
inferred: ground-storey depth 2.0 m (the back wall is in shadow; the 2018 view w22 shows it a few metres in)
right lion and the crown are behind the tree in 2022; mirrored from the left

w22-246.what: south-west return of the same end block: brick, three ribbon storeys, the open ground storey continues round the corner

w02-67.what: the 56 m Marnixstraat front: dark brick with a ground ribbon and three upper ribbons of white steel windows, the main entrance with POLITIE and the police emblem, and the open corner bay on columns
inferred: a third column seen at s 47.4 in 2024 stands behind the front row (not in the 2021 view): not modelled
emblem drawn as the police badge outline (shield with a flame), not its detail

w15-67.what: the Marnixstraat end block at the Elandsgracht corner (the tall block): brick piers, a ground hall behind a corner column, a two-storey white window block with a cantilevered balcony, a stone ledge and a two-storey glazed top under a thin roof slab that bows out over the street
w15-67.registration: s from the 2024 crop (the 2020 crop TMX7316010203-001900_pano_0004_000544 is 2.8 m off along the wall: its building edge stands at s 2.6 in open sky); y from the 2020 crop, whose roof edge matches the 3DBAG wall top (19.5 m): the 2024 heights are 0.45 m low (cornice 13.3 vs 13.95, window block 5.41 vs 5.87, 11.85 vs 12.38)

sign.kind: blue police diamond on a wall bracket, turned to the street

lantern.kind: red lantern on the brick pier (2020 crop, shifted 2.8 m); measured but not modelled: under the opening audit it read as a detached fixture

inferred: glazed-top depth: flush with the wall
roof bow 1.2 m in plan, from the 0.5 m rise of its edge in the rectified elevation

w14-247.what: the tall brick end of the west wing on the Singelgracht: blank brick with four French windows on stacked semicircular balconies
inferred: balcony projection 0.85 m (seen square-on only; the rail returns read 0.8-0.9 m against the 1.55 m doors)

w09-247.what: the quay front of the south-west wing (pink stone cladding): yellow-framed square windows on a 1.85 m pitch, a yellow-framed glazed bay, a low ribbon, a top ribbon and the stone pair on a round console

w23-248.what: framed bay in the pink stone wall on the Singelgracht
